question: What is the school type of the school with the highest latitude? Indicate the name of the school as well as the latitude coordinates.
clarification: If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
gold: SELECT c0, c1, c2 FROM (SELECT T1."School Type" AS c0, T1."School Name" AS c1, T2.Latitude AS c2, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY T2.Latitude DESC) AS __r FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode) AS __t WHERE __r <= 1
gold0: SELECT T1.`School Type`, T1.`School Name`, T2.Latitude FROM frpm AS T1 INNER JOIN schools AS T2 ON T1.CDSCode = T2.CDSCode ORDER BY T2.Latitude DESC LIMIT 1

b.request: Return the school name, school type, and latitude for every school whose latitude equals the highest latitude in the schools table, including all schools tied for highest
b.sql: SELECT s.School, f.`School Type`, s.Latitude FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN frpm AS f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE s.Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools)

d.request: What is the school type of the school with the highest latitude? Provide its name and latitude coordinates. If multiple schools tie for the highest latitude, include all of them.
d.sql: SELECT s.School AS school_name, f.`School Type` AS school_type, s.Latitude AS latitude FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN frpm AS f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE s.Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools);
